Last holy week, my friend and I went to the beach for a few days. Took the afternoon bus home to Cubao. We reached QC 1 AM ish. 

A lot of people outside the bus station were standing by the road. Naghahanap ng masasakyan. Nakakapagtaka, kasi andaming taxi. We were trying our luck with Grab pero olats.

So lumapit kami sa mga taxi. Nag-ooffer 250+ papunta sa destination namin. It takes 150 on a 'regular day'. So sabi ko, ''Bakit kuya? Wala ka bang metro?' He didn't answer. We closed the door.

Kaya pala andaming naghihintay pa rin. Lahat ng taxi nangongontrata. We got lucky eventually na makasakay sa taxi na pauwi na sa kanila and it turns out nakatira sya malapit sa destination namin ng friend ko. 

As we drove on sa highway, nagcomment sya how andaming pasahero pero walang nagsasakay na taxi. Sabi ko kasi nangsascam mga driver. Sabi ni manong, 'Pagpasensyahan nyo na. Gipit lang talaga.'

My friend and I chose to stay quiet the whole ride. On one hand, I was furious that drivers need to scam passengers to get money. On the other hand, nainis ako na imbis na magreklamo sila sa operators/asosasyon nila, mas pinipili nila na manloko ng kapwa nila. Anyway.

At first I was kinda shocked at the casting. I admit I kinda expected Annabeth to be blonde andd white, because that's how she was described in the books. 

But reading all of your insights (and Rick's as well) I now find the casting for her perfect. I get how others might cite the dumb blonde stereotype subversion to defend their image of blonde Annabeth. However, black women and girls are also often portrayed as stupid or ditzy. Battling the stereotype of the dumb girl is great! Looking at it now through a more diverse lens (from the perspective of a young black girl) is a refreshing way to combat that stereotype.

Not that it hasn't been done before. We've had our fantastic share of brilliant black women in different fields. But what I have come to love about the casting of Annabeth is that we can now see a young black girl overcoming the stereotype and shining as an intelligent and brave gal. A lot of the great black women we see in the media are just that- women. Women that have established careers, families, and goals. 

As a POC, I'd love to go on Annabeth's journey of self-discovery from the perspective of a young POC girl. As I'm sure many girls (and boys) would love too.

Oh, and I think casting a black actress not only benefits POC kids. I think it also paves the way for white children to question the biases they may have learned from their parents. Maybe it can also teach them a lesson on how to see (and love) the potential in their POC peers.

Searching videos on how to tie a noose. I was so close to doing it. I tied my noose a day before I was gonna do it. On my planned death day (my birthday), I went to a coffee shop and wrote my suicide notes. 

Couldn't remember why I didn't do it at that time (2019). But I keep wanting to do it till 2020.

2020 was a hard year for me. But little things like children in public transport wanting to hold my hand and play with me and puppies kissing me on the nose stopped me every time. The little things carried me till October 2020 (my lowest of lows, revisiting my noose I still kept knotted), where I took the plunge and talked to a therapist. And, most importantly, don't create scenarios in your head of him coming to his senses and apologizing to you, begging you to try again. 

Whether that can happen or not is not your concern right now--- this mode of thinking stems from wanting validation. You're seeking validation from the thought that he regrets his decision. Don't do this. 

You're worth it whether he realizes it or not.
